commands.name: install
commands.summary: Set up a coding agent: hooks that record its sessions, and an /agent-graph command

description.text: Set up a coding agent to work with Agent Graph. For Claude Code this does two things:

steps.text: Adds hooks to Claude Code's settings, so every new session is recorded, including sessions one starts from its shell (`claude -p`, `codex exec`, `agent-graph run`), which appear under it. Each hook runs `agent-graph emit` in the background: it takes a few milliseconds, never blocks the agent, and never sends anything anywhere. Everything else in the settings file is kept, and the old file is backed up beside it (settings.json.agent-graph.bak). Sessions that were already running aren't recorded; start a new one. Installing again brings older hooks up to date.

Adds an /agent-graph command (a skill). Run it in any session for a picture of the session and a short summary of what needs you, what looks stuck and what's in progress. `/agent-graph all` covers every session from the last day, and `/agent-graph share` gives you a live link. Claude can also use it by itself when you ask how your agents are doing.

description.text: For Codex, Gemini CLI and Cursor it adds just the command for now. Their own sessions aren't recorded yet, so it shows the Claude Code sessions that are.

table: Every project: files in your home folder. The default.
Just this project: .claude/ (or .agents/, .gemini/, .cursor/) in this folder, which you'd usually commit. Its hooks run `agent-graph` from PATH, so everyone who uses the project needs it installed.
Like project, but Claude Code's hooks go in .claude/settings.local.json, which isn't committed.

description.text: It lists what it will change and asks before writing: --yes skips the question, and --dry-run only shows the changes. Installing again changes nothing unless something is out of date. A command file of the same name that you wrote yourself is never overwritten.

commands.name: tail
commands.summary: Watch the graph live in this terminal

description.text: Watch the graph live in this terminal.

Takes over the terminal like `top` and redraws as events arrive. The top line sums everything up: how many sessions and working agents, and, in colour, how many need you, look stuck or are deadlocked. Below it, each session is a tree of its agents, most recently active first:

description.code:
claude-code:e0000002  search-indexer  [working]  Rebuilding the index schema
└─ Explore a91d0160  [working] (stale?)  Profile the slow bulk import

table: The state. idle means its turn is over and it's waiting for your next message.
It's waiting on you: a permission prompt, a question, or a plan to approve.
Working, but no events for --stale-minutes (30 by default). It may have hung or crashed, or be in one long, quiet command.
Blocked on another agent or session, with how much work is ahead of it. "looks stuck" names a stale one it's waiting on.
Sessions waiting on each other: none of them can finish.
Its task list: done out of total.
Quit. The terminal is put back as it was.
Show or hide sessions with no activity in the last day.

description.text: It checks for new events four times a second, and redraws at least every five seconds so "stale?" keeps up with the clock. Lines are cut to the terminal's width; if there are more than fit, it says how many more.
When its output isn't a terminal (piped or redirected), it prints the whole picture each time something changes instead, so it can be logged.

options.text: Follow one session: its id, the first few characters of it, or `current` (the one this runs in).
Start with sessions older than a day shown too.

commands.name: view
commands.summary: Watch the graph live in your browser, with a timeline to step through

description.text: Watch the graph live in your browser, and step back through its history.

Serves a web page on port 7777 (or --port) until you stop it with Ctrl+C, and prints its link (http://127.0.0.1:7777/?key=…), which carries a key made for this run: only someone with the link can use it, so other accounts on the machine agent-graph runs on can't. It's only reachable from that machine, and it refuses requests made by other websites. --open opens the link in your browser.

table: Every session, with anything that needs you, is deadlocked or looks stuck called out. "Older" shows sessions from before today.
The selected session's agents, what each is doing, its task progress, and what it's waiting on.
Click any session or agent: its tasks, what it's waiting on, the agents it started, its messages, and when things happened.

Every event in the session is a stop on a slider. Drag it, click it, or use ← and → to see the graph exactly as it was at that moment; the node that step changed is ringed. "Live" (or L, or End) jumps back to now.
A picture of the session as it is at the step you're on.

A Claude Code session's details have a button that reopens it in a new terminal window, in its folder (`claude --resume`). One that hasn't ended is probably still open somewhere, so that opens a copy of its conversation instead. If it can't open a window, it tells you the command to run. The shared site doesn't have this.

description.text: The page updates as events arrive, without reloading.

options.text: The port to serve on.
Open the page in your browser.

examples.text: Start it, and open it in your browser.

commands.name: snapshot
commands.summary: Save a picture of a session, sized for a phone, and print its path

description.text: Save a picture of a session and print where it went.

The picture is sized for a phone (1080 pixels wide). From the top: the session's name and state, a callout for anything that needs you, its agents as a tree (stuck ones flagged), and its task list. It's made for sharing: an agent can run this and send you the image, which is what the /agent-graph command does.

table: That session: its id, or the first few characters of it.
Every session active in the last day, one after another.
The Claude Code session this runs in, then the latest session in this folder, then the latest anywhere. This is also the default.

description.text: Only the file's path is printed, so scripts can use it. By default the picture goes in ~/.agent-graph/images/ with a new name each time. --out chooses the file, and its extension chooses the format: .png, .svg, or .json (the whole graph as data, like --json). It won't replace a file that's already there unless you add --force.

commands.name: watch-remote
commands.summary: Share the graph live on the web, and print its link

description.text: Share the graph live on the web, and print its link.

It sends the event log to the Agent Graph site (https://agentgraph.chofter.com, or --url), prints the link straight away, then sends each new event as it's recorded, until you stop it with Ctrl+C. Open the link anywhere, including on a phone: it's the same viewer as `agent-graph view`, timeline and all.

What's shared: every session on the machine agent-graph runs on, or just one with --session (`--session current` for the one this runs in). Agent Graph records task names and agent descriptions, not prompts or tool output (unless you've set AGENT_GRAPH_CAPTURE_BODIES=1). The site stores it encrypted.
Anyone with the link, unless there's a password:

table: Viewers must enter it. The site keeps only a hash.
Also use that password from now on. It's saved in ~/.agent-graph/remote.json, readable only by you.
Share this time without one, even if one's saved.

description.text: A password is only sent over HTTPS, or to your own machine.
Only this run. The site gives it a key when the log is created, every update must carry it, and it's kept only in memory.

It checks for new events once a second and sends them together. If the connection drops, new events are kept and sent when it's back. If the site refuses them outright, it stops and says why. The site deletes a log that has had no new events for a week: sharing it then stops.

options.text: The site to share on.
Viewers must enter this. `--password=` shares without one, even if a default is saved.
Save --password as the default for future runs; with an empty --password=, forget it.
Share just this session, with the sessions it started: its id, the first few characters of it, or `current` (the Claude Code session this runs in; if that isn't recorded, it stops rather than guess).

examples.text: Share every session, live. The first line printed is the link.

commands.name: run
commands.summary: Run any command as part of the graph, linked to whatever started it

description.text: Runs a command and puts it in the graph as a node of its own: working while it runs, then completed, or failed with its exit code. Its input and output pass straight through, and `run` exits with its exit code.
Use it for agents without hooks (`agent-graph run -- aider`), or for a script that starts several agents, which then appear under it.

list: Started from an agent's shell (or anywhere `AGENT_GRAPH_PARENT` is set), it goes under that session.
The command gets `AGENT_GRAPH_PARENT` and `TRACEPARENT` for the new node, so agents it starts that have Agent Graph's hooks go under it.
When a Claude Code session runs it in its shell, the session waits on it, as on any agent it starts.

description.text: Put the command after `--`, so its own options aren't read as `run`'s.

options.text: What to call it in the graph. Defaults to the program's name.
The command to run, and its arguments.

examples.text: Aider has no hooks: this shows it in the graph while it runs.
Group the sessions a script starts under one node called nightly.
A headless Claude Code session, under a node that records how it exited.
